appearance_facts.fact: Chart title is 'Monthly Grid Energy Use (kWh)' in bold black text at the top center.
Y-axis label is 'Grid energy use (kWh)' in black text, aligned left.
X-axis label is 'Month' in black text, centered below the bars.
X-axis has labeled ticks for 'Apr', 'Jan', 'Jun', 'Feb', 'Mar', and 'May', from left to right.
All bars are solid dark red.
Bars are rectangular, aligned with their respective month labels on the x-axis.
Bar heights correspond to energy use values: Jan ~40,000 kWh, Apr ~30,000 kWh, Mar ~27,000 kWh, Feb ~20,000 kWh, Jun ~18,000 kWh, and May ~8,000 kWh.

printed_facts.fact: Y-axis scale is in kWh, with grid lines at 10,000, 15,000, 20,000, 25,000, 30,000, 35,000, and 40,000.
X-axis labels are 'Apr', 'Jan', 'Jun', 'Feb', 'Mar', and 'May', in that order from left to right.
Bar heights indicate energy use: Jan ~40,000 kWh, Apr ~30,000 kWh, Mar ~27,000 kWh, Feb ~20,000 kWh, Jun ~18,000 kWh, and May ~8,000 kWh.
The bar for May is the shortest, at approximately 8,000 kWh, visually below the 10,000 kWh grid line.

public_definitions: The goal is to review the monthly grid energy dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-usage case or escalated as a critical low-usage anomaly for this reporting cycle.
The chart is the evidence source for deciding the appropriate May low-usage severity route.
The options are: Route May to standard low-usage follow-up, Escalate May to critical low-usage anomaly review, or Send May to background monthly record filing.
